# Tapir commands: Project Commands

The 70 commands of this group, with their parameters, results and examples. Every group and how a command is sent: [commands.md](https://archicad-api.com/commands.md).

## Project Commands

### GetProjectInfo

Retrieves information about the currently loaded project.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 0.1.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetProjectInfo

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `isUntitled` (boolean, required): True, if the project is not saved yet.
- `isTeamwork` (boolean, required): True, if the project is a Teamwork (BIMcloud) project.
- `projectLocation` (string): The location of the project in the filesystem or a BIMcloud project reference. A BIMcloud project reference is returned without the user name and login token.
- `projectPath` (string): The path of the project. A filesystem path or a BIMcloud server relative path.
- `projectName` (string): The name of the project.

Grasshopper: `GetProjectInfoComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetProjectInfo.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetProjectInfo.py): Prints the name, path and Teamwork state of the open project with GetProjectInfo.

Parameters:

- `projectInfoFields` (array of ProjectInfoFieldData, required): Array of custom project info fields to create.

Returns:

- `fields` (CreatedProjectInfoFieldsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateProjectInfoFieldsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/CreateProjectInfoFields.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/CreateProjectInfoFields.py): Creates a custom Project Info field with CreateProjectInfoFields, then deletes it again. From Archicad 30 the new field goes to the first Project Info group unless projectInfoGroupId is given.

### DeleteProjectInfoFields

Deletes one or more custom project info fields, by their autotext keys or, from Archicad 30, by the ids of the fields of the Project Info groups. Hardcoded fields cannot be deleted.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.4. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteProjectInfoFields

Parameters:

- `projectInfoIds` (array of string): List of project info field ids (autotext keys, as GetProjectInfoFields returns them) to delete. Only custom fields can be deleted. On Archicad 30 a key is matched to the field by its name, so it fails when more than one field has the name; delete such a field by its projectInfoFieldId instead.
- `projectInfoFieldIds` (array of ProjectInfoFieldIdArrayItem): List of fields of the Project Info groups to delete, by the ids GetProjectInfoGroups returns. Available from Archicad 30. Their results follow the results of projectInfoIds.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `DeleteProjectInfoFieldsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/DeleteProjectInfoFields.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/DeleteProjectInfoFields.py): Creates a custom Project Info field and deletes it by its autotext key with DeleteProjectInfoFields. Built-in fields cannot be deleted. From Archicad 30 fields can also be deleted by projectInfoFieldIds.

### RenameProjectInfoFields

Renames custom fields of the Project Info groups. Fixed (built-in) fields cannot be renamed. Available from Archicad 30.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RenameProjectInfoFields

Parameters:

- `projectInfoFields` (array of object, required): The fields of the Project Info groups to rename, each with its new name. Fixed (built-in) fields cannot be renamed.
  - `projectInfoFieldId` (ProjectInfoFieldId, required)
  - `name` (string, required): The new name of the field. It must not be used by another field.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `RenameProjectInfoFieldsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/RenameProjectInfoFields.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/RenameProjectInfoFields.py): Creates a custom Project Info field, renames it with RenameProjectInfoFields, then deletes it. Built-in fields cannot be renamed. Requires Archicad 30 or later.

### MoveProjectInfoFields

Moves fields of the Project Info groups to a group, before another field of it or to its end. A subfield of a calculated field moves with its parent field. Available from Archicad 30.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#MoveProjectInfoFields

Parameters:

- `projectInfoFields` (array of object, required): The fields of the Project Info groups to move, in the order the moves are made. A subfield of a calculated field cannot be moved on its own, it moves with its parent field.
  - `projectInfoFieldId` (ProjectInfoFieldId, required)
  - `projectInfoGroupId` (ProjectInfoGroupId, required): The group to move the field to. To reorder a field within its group, give its current group.
  - `beforeProjectInfoFieldId` (ProjectInfoFieldId): The field of the target group to move the field before. When omitted, the field is moved to the end of the group.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `MoveProjectInfoFieldsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/MoveProjectInfoFields.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/MoveProjectInfoFields.py): Creates a custom Project Info field, moves it to the top of the first group with MoveProjectInfoFields, then deletes it. Requires Archicad 30 or later.

### GetStories

Retrieves information about the story structure of the currently loaded project: index, floor id, name, level, height and, from Archicad 28, the IFC GlobalId of each story.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.5. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetStories

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `firstStory` (integer, required): First story index.
- `lastStory` (integer, required): Last story index.
- `actStory` (integer, required): Actual (currently visible in 2D) story index.
- `skipNullFloor` (boolean, required): Floor indices above ground-floor level may start with 1 instead of 0.
- `stories` (StoriesParameters, required)

Grasshopper: `GetDetailsOfElementsComponent`, `GetStoriesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetStories.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetStories.py): Prints the stories of the project (index, name, level, height) with GetStories.

### SetStories

Sets the story structure of the currently loaded project to the given list of stories. Existing stories outside the list are deleted, and Archicad deletes every element whose home story they are with them; dryRun lists those stories with the number of elements on each, without changing anything. To add, change or delete a single story, use InsertStory or DeleteStory instead.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.5. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetStories

Parameters:

- `stories` (StoriesSettings, required)
- `dryRun` (DryRun): If true, nothing is changed in the project and no undo step is created: the list is checked as in a real run, and the response lists the existing stories a real run would delete (with the number of elements Archicad would delete with each) and the number of stories it would insert. Default is false.

Returns:

- `success` (boolean, required): Whether the story structure was set, or on a dry run, whether the list passed the checks a real run makes first.
- `error` (Error)
- `wouldDeleteStories` (array of object): Only on a successful dry run: the existing stories a real run would delete, from the bottom up. Empty when it would delete none.
  - `index` (integer, required): The index of the story.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the story.
  - `elementCount` (integer, required): The number of elements whose home story is the story (in the floor plan database): Archicad deletes them together with it.
- `wouldInsertStoryCount` (integer): Only on a successful dry run: the number of new stories a real run would add below and above the existing ones until they reach the requested indices. When the requested indices leave a gap above or below the existing stories, this includes the stories in the gap, which the real run deletes again.
- `dryRun` (DryRunFlag)

Grasshopper: `SetStoriesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SetStories.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SetStories.py): Renames the top story with SetStories, reads the stories back, then restores the original names. SetStories takes the whole story structure: stories left out are deleted, new ones are created. A dry run first shows what leaving out the top story would delete (the story and the number of elements on it) without changing anything.

### InsertStory

Inserts one new story directly above or below an existing story, with its name, height and level line display, and returns the new story as GetStories reports it. Other stories are never deleted; their indices and levels can change with the insertion as in Archicad's Story Settings dialog, so read them again with GetStories.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#InsertStory

Parameters:

- `storyIndex` (integer, required): The index of an existing story (see GetStories) next to which the new story is inserted.
- `position` (string ("Above", "Below"), required): Whether the new story is inserted directly above or directly below the story of storyIndex.
- `name` (string): The name of the new story. Default is an empty name.
- `height` (number): The height of the new story, greater than zero. Default is the height of the story of storyIndex.
- `dispOnSections` (boolean): Whether the level line of the new story appears on sections and elevations. Default is what Archicad gives a new story.

Returns:

- `story` (StoryParameters, required): The new story, as GetStories reports it after the insertion.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/InsertStory.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/InsertStory.py): Inserts a new story above the top story with InsertStory, prints it, then deletes it again with DeleteStory. Unlike SetStories, InsertStory only adds a story; no other story is deleted.

### DeleteStory

Deletes one story. Archicad deletes every element whose home story it is together with it, so a story that is the home story of any element is only deleted with deleteElements: true; otherwise it fails and gives the number of those elements. dryRun reports, without changing anything, whether the story would be deleted and how many elements with it.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteStory

Parameters:

- `storyIndex` (integer, required): The index of the story to delete (see GetStories).
- `deleteElements` (boolean): Archicad deletes every element whose home story is the deleted story. Without true here, a story that is the home story of any element is not deleted, and the response says how many elements it has. Default is false.
- `dryRun` (DryRun)

Returns:

- `success` (boolean, required): Whether the story was deleted, or on a dry run, whether a real run would delete it.
- `error` (Error)
- `wouldDelete` (boolean (true)): Present, and true, on a dry run that a real run would delete the story.
- `elementCount` (integer): The number of elements whose home story is the story (in the floor plan database): the elements deleted with it, or that kept it from being deleted. Absent when the story was not found.
- `dryRun` (DryRunFlag)

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/DeleteStory.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/DeleteStory.py): Inserts a story, places a wall on it, and deletes the story with DeleteStory. A story that is the home story of elements is only deleted with deleteElements: true, because Archicad deletes those elements with it. A dry run first tells how many elements that would be.

### ModifyStory

Changes the name, level, height or level line display of one story, and returns the story as GetStories reports it. It never adds or deletes a story. level moves only this story; height moves every story above with the top of this one, as in Archicad's Story Settings dialog. The elements of a moved story move with it.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyStory

Parameters:

- `storyIndex` (integer, required): The index of the story to modify (see GetStories).
- `name` (string): The new name of the story.
- `level` (number): The new level of the story. Only this story moves: the story below gets taller or shorter, and the stories above stay where they are unless height is given too. It must stay above the level of the story below, and, without height, below the level of the story above. On the top story without height its top stays where it is: moving it up makes it shorter by as much, and moving it down taller.
- `height` (number): The new height of the story, greater than zero. As in Archicad's Story Settings dialog, every story above moves up or down with the top of this story and keeps its height.
- `dispOnSections` (boolean): Whether the level line of the story appears on sections and elevations.

Returns:

- `story` (StoryParameters, required): The modified story, as GetStories reports it after the change.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/ModifyStory.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/ModifyStory.py): Inserts a story above the top story, renames it, changes its height and level with ModifyStory, then deletes it again. Unlike SetStories, ModifyStory changes one story and never adds or deletes one. A new height moves the stories above with the top of the story; a new level moves only the story itself.

### GetAutoTextKeys

Retrieves the available autotext keys (name and embeddable key): the Project Info, layout, drawing, date and other autotexts Archicad lists, and the property based ones, optionally for a specific element. Embed a key in a Text or Label content by surrounding it with '<' and '>'.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.9. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetAutoTextKeys

Parameters:

- `elementId` (ElementId): Optional. The element to retrieve context dependent autotext keys for (its own properties, plus the ones common to all element types, e.g. 'Element ID', 'Area'). When omitted, only the property based autotext keys common to all element types are returned. The other autotexts (Project Info, layout, drawing, date, ...) are returned either way.

Returns:

- `autoTextKeys` (array of object, required)
  - `name` (string, required): The autotext's name, as shown in the Insert Autotext dialog of Archicad.
  - `key` (string, required): The autotext's key. To embed it in the content of a Text or Label element, surround it with '<' and '>', e.g. '<PROJECTNAME>' or '<PROPERTY-69A58F6F-DD3B-478D-B5EF-09A16BD0C548>'.

Grasshopper: `GetAutoTextKeysComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetAutoTextKeys.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetAutoTextKeys.py): Prints the autotext keys (name and key) that a Text or Label can embed as <KEY>, with GetAutoTextKeys. Pass an elementId to get the keys of that element's type as well.

### InterpretAutoTexts

Resolves one or more autotexts (e.g. '<LAYOUTID>') to their values, optionally in the context of an element, so a key can be tested before it is written into a Text or Label.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#InterpretAutoTexts

Parameters:

- `autoTexts` (array of string, required): The autotexts to resolve, either as they are written in the content of a Text or Label element, e.g. '<LAYOUTID>' or '<PROPERTY-69A58F6F-DD3B-478D-B5EF-09A16BD0C548>', or as bare keys without the surrounding '<' and '>', e.g. 'LAYOUTID'.
- `elementId` (ElementId): Optional. The element in whose context the autotexts are resolved, e.g. a Text on a layout for layout autotexts. When omitted, they are resolved without an element context.

Returns:

- `values` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): One result per input autotext, in the same order.

Grasshopper: `InterpretAutoTextsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/InterpretAutoTexts.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/InterpretAutoTexts.py): Resolves the project name autotext to its value with InterpretAutoTexts. An autotext can be given as written in a Text ('<PROJECTNAME>') or as a bare key ('PROJECTNAME'). Pass an elementId (e.g. of a Text on a layout) to resolve them in that element's context.

### GetNoteAutotexts

Retrieves the autotexts available in the notes of an element type (e.g. a Dimension), each with the element types it is available for. The autotexts are identified by the numeric value of their API_NoteAutotextID. For a Dimension, the optional dimensionAppearance (Linear by default) chooses the dimension type. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetNoteAutotexts

Parameters:

- `noteOwnerType` (ElementType, required): The type of the element that owns the note, e.g. 'Dimension', 'RadialDimension', 'LevelDimension' or 'AngleDimension'.
- `dimensionAppearance` (string ("Linear", "Cumulative", "Baseline", "Elevation")): Optional dimension type, as in the Dimension Settings, whose note autotexts are listed when noteOwnerType is 'Dimension'. Defaults to Linear. Not allowed with other owner types.

Returns:

- `noteAutotexts` (array of NoteAutotextDetails, required): The autotexts available in the notes of the given owner type, in ascending order of autotextId.

Grasshopper: `GetNoteAutotextsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetNoteAutotexts.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetNoteAutotexts.py): Prints the autotexts available in the notes of linear and of elevation dimensions, with GetNoteAutotexts. For noteOwnerType 'Dimension' the optional dimensionAppearance (Linear, Cumulative, Baseline or Elevation) chooses the dimension type; it defaults to Linear. Requires Archicad 26 or later.

### GetHotlinks

Gets the file system locations (path) of the hotlink modules and the instance elements placed from each node. The hotlinks can have tree hierarchy in the project.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 0.1.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetHotlinks

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `hotlinks` (Hotlinks, required)

Grasshopper: `GetHotLinksComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetHotlinks.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetHotlinks.py): Prints the hotlink nodes of the project (source file, name, type, placed instances and children) with GetHotlinks.

### CreateHotlinkNodes

Creates hotlink module nodes from source files. A node that already points at the same file is returned instead of duplicated (Archicad 26 and later; 25 cannot see an unplaced node).

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.9. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateHotlinkNodes

Parameters:

- `hotlinkNodes` (array of object, required): The hotlink module nodes to create. A node that already points at the same source file (compared case-insensitively) is returned as it is, with existing: true, and the name and story settings asked for are ignored. On Archicad 25 a node that has not been placed yet cannot be found, so a repeated request there creates a second node.
  - `sourceLocation` (string, required): Absolute path of the module source file (.mod or .pln).
  - `name` (string): Optional display name of the node. Defaults to the file name. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.
  - `storyRangeType` (string ("AllStories", "SingleStory")): Optional. Which stories of the source are placed: all of them, or the single reference story. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.
  - `refFloorIndex` (integer): Optional index of the reference story in the source file. Defaults to 0. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

Returns:

- `hotlinkNodes` (array of HotlinkNodeCreatedOrError, required): One item per requested node, in order: the node guid with its existing flag, or an error.

Grasshopper: `CreateHotlinkNodesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/CreateHotlinkNodes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/CreateHotlinkNodes.py): Saves the first wall as a module in the temp folder, creates a hotlink node from it with CreateHotlinkNodes, then deletes the node. Needs at least one Wall.

The node is made from the first wall, saved as a module in the temp folder; at the end the node is deleted with its instance. Needs at least one Wall.

### MergeFile

Merges an Archicad project or module file into the model, as File > Interoperability > Merge does, at an origin, rotation and mirroring, each story of the file on the story with the same index (or from floorIndex on). The Archicad API has no merge, so the file is placed as a hotlink and the hotlink is broken, in one undo step, and the elements that are new afterwards are returned; Archicad leaves them grouped together. A file the project already hotlinks is refused, because breaking would break that hotlink too.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#MergeFile

Parameters:

- `sourceLocation` (string, required): Absolute path of the file to merge: an Archicad project (.pln, .pla) or module (.mod). It cannot be a file the project already hotlinks: breaking that hotlink would turn its placed instances into ordinary elements too.
- `origin` (HotlinkOrigin): Optional. Where the origin of the file lands in the project. Defaults to the project origin; if z is omitted, it is 0.
- `rotationAngle` (number): Optional rotation about the origin, counter-clockwise, in radians. Defaults to 0.
- `mirrored` (boolean): Optional. Reflects the file's local X axis before the rotation. Defaults to false.
- `floorIndex` (integer): Optional story of the project that the story with index 0 of the file goes to; the other stories of the file follow it. Defaults to 0, so each story of the file goes to the story with the same index.

Returns:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements the merge added to the model, every element of the file's model. Archicad leaves them grouped together, as it leaves the elements of a broken hotlink; UngroupElements dissolves the group.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/MergeFile.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/MergeFile.py): Merges a module file into the project with MergeFile, 10 m north of where it was saved. The script saves a wall it creates as a module in a temporary folder first; the wall and the merged elements are deleted at the end. Requires Archicad 27 or later (SaveAsModuleFile with an element list).

Needs a saved, non-Teamwork project. Discards unsaved changes without asking.

Closes the currently opened project. Fails, instead of answering success, when Archicad leaves the project open, as it does with its last open project.

Closes the project. Save it first. When Archicad keeps the project open (as it does with its last open project), the command fails and says so instead of answering success.

### SaveProject

Saves the currently opened project, in place or to a given path. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file at the path.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.3.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SaveProject

Parameters:

- `projectPath` (string): Optional. Full path of a .pln file to save the project to, as File > Save As does: the open project then refers to that file. This saves an untitled project, or one opened from an older Archicad version, which cannot be saved in place. An existing file at the path is overwritten, unless overwrite is false. When omitted, or when it is the project's own file, the project is saved in place, which keeps the refusal of a project opened read-only.
- `overwrite` (boolean): Optional, true by default. Only together with projectPath: false refuses to save when a file already exists at projectPath, the project's own file included, and writes nothing.


Grasshopper: `SaveProjectComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SaveProject.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SaveProject.py): Saves the open project to its file with SaveProject. Overwrites the project file with the current state. An untitled project needs projectPath.

### SaveProjectAsArchive

Saves the open project as an archive (.pla) file, with the library parts it uses inside. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file.

- `includeTextures` (boolean): Optional, false by default. Whether the linked textures go into the archive.
- `includeBackgroundPicture` (boolean): Optional, false by default. Whether the background picture goes into the archive.

### PhotoRender

Renders the 3D model with the current rendering scene, or with the given one, as Document > Creative Imaging > PhotoRender Projection does, and saves the image to a file (png, jpg, bmp, tiff or gif). The image size, resolution and quality come from the scene; a width, height or resolution given here is used for this render only, the scene is not changed. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file; a folder that does not exist is refused before rendering.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#PhotoRender

Parameters:

- `imageFilePath` (string, required): Absolute path of the image file to write. Its folder must exist: a missing folder is refused before anything is rendered. An existing file is overwritten, unless overwrite is false.
- `overwrite` (boolean): Optional, true by default. false refuses to render when a file already exists at imageFilePath, and writes nothing.
- `format` (string ("png", "jpg", "bmp", "tiff", "gif")): Optional. The image file format; omitted, it comes from the extension of imageFilePath (.png, .jpg or .jpeg, .bmp, .tif or .tiff, .gif).
- `sceneName` (string): Optional. The rendering scene to render with, one of the names GetRenderingScenes returns. It is made the current scene first, as SetCurrentRenderingScene does, and stays current afterwards. Omitted, the current scene is used.
- `width` (integer): Optional. The width of the image in pixels (the Size field of the PhotoRendering Settings palette). Omitted, the width of the scene is used. The image settings of the scene are changed for this render only and restored afterwards.
- `height` (integer): Optional. The height of the image in pixels (the Size field of the PhotoRendering Settings palette). Omitted, the height of the scene is used. The image settings of the scene are changed for this render only and restored afterwards.
- `resolution` (integer): Optional. The resolution of the image in dpi (the Resolution field of the PhotoRendering Settings palette). Omitted, the resolution of the scene is used. The image settings of the scene are changed for this render only and restored afterwards.


Grasshopper: `PhotoRenderComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/PhotoRender.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/PhotoRender.py): Renders the 3D model with the current rendering scene into a 640x480 png in the temp folder with PhotoRender. The model is rendered as the 3D window shows it. The scene's own size and resolution are not changed.

- `format` (string ("png", "jpg", "bmp", "tiff", "gif")): Optional. The image file format; omitted, it comes from the extension of imageFilePath (.png, .jpg or .jpeg, .bmp, .tif or .tiff, .gif).
- `colorDepth` (string ("blackAndWhite", "16Colors", "256Colors", "16Grays", "256Grays", "trueColor", "trueColorWithAlpha")): Optional, trueColor by default. The color depth of the image, as in the Save as picture dialog.

### GetProjectPreferences

Gets pages of the project preferences (Options > Project Preferences): the working units, the dimensions, the calculation units, the zones and the reference levels, and the Floor Plan Cut Plane Settings. Further pages may follow.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetProjectPreferences

Parameters:

- `preferenceTypes` (array of string ("WorkingUnits", "Dimensions", "CalculationUnits", "Zones", "ReferenceLevels", "FloorPlanCutPlane")): The preference pages to get. Every page when missing.

Returns:

- `workingUnits` (object): The Working Units page: the units and the number of decimals the model's lengths, areas, volumes and angles are shown with.
  - `length` (object, required)
  - `area` (object, required)
  - `volume` (object, required)
  - `angle` (object, required)
- `dimensions` (object): The Dimensions page: the dimension standard and the format (unit, decimals, extra accuracy and zero handling) of each dimension type.
  - `dimensionStandardIndex` (integer, required): The index of the dimension standard the page follows.
  - `linear` (object, required): The format of the linear dimensions.
  - `angle` (object, required): The format of the angle dimensions.
  - `radial` (object, required): The format of the radial dimensions.
  - `level` (object, required): The format of the level dimensions.
  - `elevation` (object, required): The format of the elevation dimensions.
  - `doorWindow` (object, required): The format of the door, window and skylight dimensions.
  - `parapet` (object, required): The format of the sill height (parapet) dimensions.
  - `area` (object, required): The format of the area values the dimensions show (area calculations).
- `calculationUnits` (object): The Calculation Units page: the units, the number of decimals and the extra accuracy of the values in element lists and schedules. GetCalculationUnits answers the same page.
  - `length` (object, required)
  - `area` (object, required)
  - `volume` (object, required)
  - `angle` (object, required)
- `zones` (object): The Zones page: the reduction of the calculated zone area under a low ceiling. The wall inset (niche) sizes of the page are not available through the API.
  - `lowCeilingAreaReduction` (object, required): Up to three ceiling height limits split a zone into height ranges; the area of each range is reduced by its own percent in the calculated area of the zone.
- `referenceLevels` (object): The Reference Levels page: two named levels that elevations can be measured from, besides Project Zero and the stories.
  - `level1` (object, required): The first reference level.
  - `level2` (object, required): The second reference level.
- `floorPlanCutPlane` (object): The Floor Plan Cut Plane Settings (Document > Floor Plan Cut Plane): where the floor plan cuts the model and which range of it the floor plan shows.
  - `cutPlaneHeight` (number, required): The height of the cut plane from the current story in meters.
  - `topLevel` (object, required): The top of the floor plan range: elements are shown up to this level.
  - `bottomLevel` (object, required): The bottom of the floor plan range: elements are shown down to this level.
  - `absoluteDisplayLimit` (number, required): The absolute display limit from Project Zero in meters: elements set to show on the floor plan down to the absolute display limit are shown down to this level.

Grasshopper: `GetProjectPreferencesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetProjectPreferences.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetProjectPreferences.py): Prints the working units, the reference levels and the floor plan cut plane with GetProjectPreferences. Without preferenceTypes every page is returned.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/RebuildView.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/RebuildView.py): Rebuilds and regenerates the current view with RebuildView.

### GetAutoIntersect

Gets whether Auto-Intersection (Options > Auto-Intersection) is on. It changes what the wall and beam creation commands produce: with it on, the new elements are joined at their intersections.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetAutoIntersect

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `isOn` (boolean, required): True if Auto-Intersection is currently on.

Grasshopper: `GetAutoIntersectComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetAutoIntersect.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetAutoIntersect.py): Prints whether Auto-Intersection (Options > Auto-Intersection) is on with GetAutoIntersect.

### SetAutoIntersect

Turns Auto-Intersection on or off. It is a setting of the running Archicad, not of the project; remember to restore the previous state afterwards.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetAutoIntersect

Parameters:

- `isOn` (boolean, required): Turn Auto-Intersection on or off.


Grasshopper: `SetAutoIntersectComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SetAutoIntersect.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SetAutoIntersect.py): Turns Auto-Intersection off with SetAutoIntersect, reads it back, then restores the previous state. It is a setting of the running Archicad, not of the project.

### ResolveNames

Looks up words or phrases (for example from a user's question) among the names of the open project before they are passed to other commands: stories, layers, layer combinations, building materials, composites, profiles, surfaces, fills, lines, zone categories, element types (by API name and, from Archicad 27, by the name the Archicad interface shows), properties (by name, and by group and name together) and classifications (systems by name and version, items of every system by name and ID). For each name it returns 'found' with the items named exactly so, 'closeMatches' with the nearest names, best first (ranked by differences in case, accents, spacing and separators, shared words, one name containing the other and a few differing characters), or 'notFound' when nothing in the project is close, meaning the project has no such item and it must not be guessed. Each match carries what the other commands take: the story index, the attribute id and index, the elementType, the propertyId (with the property's group, value type and the classification items a custom property is available for), or the classificationSystemId and classificationItemId. Matching is lexical and deterministic. Read only.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ResolveNames

Parameters:

- `names` (array of object, required): The words or phrases to look up in the open project, for example taken from a user's question.
  - `name` (string, required): The word or phrase.
  - `kind` (NameKind): The kind of item the word names. When it is left out, every kind is searched.
- `maxCloseMatches` (integer): The most close matches returned for one word, best first. The default is 5.

Returns:

- `results` (array of object, required): One result for each of the given names, in the same order.
  - `name` (string, required): The given word or phrase.
  - `status` (string ("found", "closeMatches", "notFound"), required): found: an item of the project has exactly this name (see found). closeMatches: no item has exactly this name, but some are close (see closeMatches). notFound: nothing in the project is close to it; the project has no such item, so it must not be guessed.
  - `found` (array of NameMatch, required): The items named exactly so (the same characters), with match 'exact'. More than one when items of different kinds, or several stories, have the name.
  - `closeMatches` (array of NameMatch, required): When nothing is named exactly so: the nearest items, best first. Empty when the status is found or notFound.

Grasshopper: `ResolveNamesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/ResolveNames.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/ResolveNames.py): Checks words from a user's question against the open project with ResolveNames before using them: a story, a building material, an element type, a property, a classification and a word looked up among every kind of name. Each result says whether the project has an item named exactly so (found), only similar names (closeMatches, best first) or nothing close (notFound). A matched property carries the propertyId that GetPropertyValuesOfElements takes, a matched classification item its classificationSystemId and classificationItemId.

### HotlinkInstanceChange

object
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `origin` (HotlinkOrigin): If z is omitted, the instance's current z is kept.
- `rotationAngle` (number): Rotation about the origin, counter-clockwise, in radians.
- `mirrored` (boolean): Reflect the module's local X axis before the rotation.
- `floorDifference` (integer)
- `skipNested` (boolean)
- `suspendFixAngle` (boolean)
- `ignoreTopFloorLinks` (boolean)
- `relinkWallOpenings` (boolean)
- `adjustLevelDiffs` (boolean)
- `layerIndex` (integer): Move the instance to this layer. A layerIndex that is not a layer of the project is refused.

### HotlinkInstanceCreation

object
- `hotlinkNodeId` (HotlinkNodeId, required): The node to place, from GetHotlinks or CreateHotlinkNodes. On Archicad 25 a node that has never been placed cannot be read, so a node created through the API can only be placed from Archicad 26 on.
- `origin` (HotlinkOrigin, required): If z is omitted, the instance is placed at 0.
- `rotationAngle` (number): Optional rotation about the origin, counter-clockwise, in radians. Defaults to 0.
- `mirrored` (boolean): Optional. Reflects the module's local X axis before the rotation. Defaults to false.
- `floorIndex` (integer): Optional story the instance is placed on. Defaults to the current story.
- `floorDifference` (integer): Optional story offset applied to the module's stories. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer of the instance. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default layer, or to the built-in Archicad layer when that layer has been deleted. A layerIndex that is not a layer of the project is refused.
- `skipNested` (boolean): Optional. Do not place hotlinks nested inside the module. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `suspendFixAngle` (boolean): Optional. Rotate fixed-angle elements with the module. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `ignoreTopFloorLinks` (boolean): Optional. Top-linked elements keep their height rather than their top story link. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `relinkWallOpenings` (boolean): Optional. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `adjustLevelDiffs` (boolean): Optional. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.

The topmost story gets its height from the virtual story that Archicad keeps above it in the story settings; only an Archicad that did not report that virtual story would leave the top story without a height.

When given for more than one story, the indices must be consecutive.

### CalculationUnitVolumeFormat

object
- `unit` (VolumeType, required)
- `accuracy` (AccuracyType, required)
- `decimals` (integer, required): Number of decimals to display for volume values.

### NameKind

string ("Story", "Layer", "LayerCombination", "BuildingMaterial", "Composite", "Profile", "Surface", "Fill", "Line", "ZoneCategory", "ElementType", "Property", ...): The kind of an item of the project that ResolveNames looks a name up among: a story, an attribute of the given type, an element type (matched by its API name and, from Archicad 27, by the name the Archicad interface shows), a property (built-in or custom; matched by its name and by its group and name together), or a classification (a classification system, matched by its name and by its name and version together, or an item of any system at any depth, matched by its name, by its ID and by both together).

### NameMatch

object: An item of the project that a name matches, as ResolveNames returns it.
- `kind` (NameKind, required)
- `name` (string, required): The name of the item in the project. For an element type, the name the Archicad interface shows (from Archicad 27; the API name before). For a classification item, its name, or its ID when it has no name.
- `match` (string ("exact", "normalized", "words", "contains", "similar"), required): How the name matches. exact: the same characters. normalized: the same except for case, accents, spacing and separators (FireRating, fire_rating, Fire Rating). words: every word of one is a word of the other, or at least half of their words are shared. contains: one contains the other. similar: a few characters differ.
- `score` (number, required): How close the match is, from 0.6 to 1 (1 for exact and normalized matches).
- `storyIndex` (integer): The index of the story (the floor index the commands take). Only for a story.
- `level` (number): The level of the story, in meters. Only for a story.
- `attributeId` (AttributeId)
- `attributeIndex` (integer): The index of the attribute. Only for an attribute.
- `elementType` (ElementType)
- `propertyId` (PropertyId): The property, as GetPropertyValuesOfElements and SetPropertyValuesOfElements take it. Only for a property.
- `propertyGroupId` (PropertyGroupId): The group of the property. Only for a property.
- `propertyGroupName` (string): The name of the group of the property. Only for a property.
- `propertyType` (string ("StaticBuiltIn", "DynamicBuiltIn", "Custom")): Whether the property is built in or custom. Only for a property.
- `propertyCollectionType` (string ("Undefined", "Single", "List", "SingleChoiceEnumeration", "MultipleChoiceEnumeration")): Whether the property holds one value, a list, or one or more choices of a list of options. Only for a property.
- `propertyValueType` (string ("Undefined", "Integer", "Real", "String", "Boolean", "Guid")): The type of the values of the property. Only for a property.
- `propertyMeasureType` (string ("Undefined", "Default", "Length", "Area", "Volume", "Angle")): What a number value of the property measures. Only for a property; left out for the attribute index types of some built-in properties.
- `propertyIsEditable` (boolean): Whether the value of the property can be set. Only for a property.
- `availability` (ClassificationItemIds): The classification items the property is available for: an element has the property only when it is classified as one of them. Only for a custom property; built-in properties have no such list.
- `classificationSystemId` (ClassificationSystemId): The classification system, or the system of the classification item. Only for a classification.
- `classificationSystemName` (string): The name of the classification system. Only for a classification.
- `classificationItemId` (ClassificationItemId): The classification item. Only for a classification item, not for a classification system.
- `classificationItemCode` (string): The ID of the classification item, as Archicad shows it (for example Ss_25_10). Only for a classification item.
